the observed luminosities in the H{alpha}, FUV, and FUV - H{alpha} color are consistent with a universal IMF convolved with a cluster mass function, but inconsistent with an IMF that truncates at the high-mass end.

a universal IMF, convolved with the CMF, reproduces all observations in this paper, while the IGIMF fails to do so.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the observed H{beta} luminosity is the product of a universal IMF, the cluster mass function, and the star formation rate.
we have shown that stochastic star formation can explain the H{alpha}/FUV ratio in dwarf and low SFR galaxies.
the stochastic sampling of star clusters can explain the observed luminosity ratio between the FUV and H{alpha} emission in galaxies, even when the IMF is universal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stochastic sampling of the IMF in star clusters and in galaxies can explain the observed Hα to FUV ratio at low star formation rate (SFR) without invoking a truncated or steepened IMF.
stochastic sampling of stars in galaxies is important at low star formation rate (SFR).
the observed distribution of H{alpha} in dwarf galaxies is the result of a universal IMF, random sampling, and the CMF.
